@@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S14.p4" data-s="0" data-ev>@@Here @@html:<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>&#x00393;</mi></mrow></math>@@ bounds the size of the thrust, so its integral times @@html:<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>&#x0002F;</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></mrow></math>@@ is the nitrogen used; @@html:<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>@@ is what the tank can give, the measured 76 kN peak while the tank is above the regulator's 20 MPa and less once it is not, the tilt limit @@html:<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>&#x003B8;</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>@@ is 15° and the touchdown speed @@html:<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>@@ is 1 m/s.@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S14.p4" data-s="1" data-ev>@@Every constraint is linear or a cone, so the problem is convex[fn:: An engine that cannot throttle below @@html:<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>@@ makes the constraint @@html:<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&#x02264;</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>&#x02016;</mo><mi>&#x1D42E;</mi><mo>&#x02016;</mo></mrow></math>@@ non-convex. Açıkmeşe and Ploen replace the thrust's size by a slack @@html:<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>&#x00393;</mi></mrow></math>@@, with @@html:<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>&#x02016;</mo><mi>&#x1D42E;</mi><mo>&#x02016;</mo><mo>&#x02264;</mo><mi>&#x00393;</mi></mrow></math>@@ and @@html:<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&#x0002F;</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>&#x02264;</mo><mi>&#x00393;</mi></mrow></math>@@, which is convex, and prove that at the optimum @@html:<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>&#x02016;</mo><mi>&#x1D42E;</mi><mo>&#x02016;</mo><mo>&#x0003D;</mo><mi>&#x00393;</mi></mrow></math>@@, so the relaxation loses nothing. My version has no minimum thrust, so @@html:<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>&#x00393;</mi></mrow></math>@@ only names the thrust's size.] and a solver finds its optimum in milliseconds.@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S14.p4" data-s="2" data-ev>@@The controller wraps it in a loop: every 0.2 s it measures @@html:<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>&#x1D42B;</mi></mrow></math>@@ and @@html:<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>&#x1D42F;</mi></mrow></math>@@, solves the problem for final times @@html:<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>f</mi></msub></mrow></math>@@ from 0.2 to 3.2 s, keeps the plan that uses the least nitrogen, flies the first 0.2 s of it, and plans again.@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S14.p4" data-s="3" data-ev>@@When the tank cools as it empties, the thrust limit depends on how much gas the plan itself uses, which is not convex.@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S14.p4" data-s="4" data-ev>@@The controller solves with the limit the tank gives now, recomputes the limit along the plan's own gas use, and solves again until the two agree: a small case of successive convexification.@@html:</span>@@

animation needs JavaScript; the figure below shows the same flights.</p></noscript></div><figcaption>The model-predictive descent replayed, one plan at a time. Bold dashed blue: the plan the MPC is flying, solved from the state at that moment; faint dashed: its earlier plans; solid blue: the path flown so far; dotted: the thrust the tank can still give. Orange: the PID's sink-rate law from the same state. Each new plan lands at the same moment as the one before, because the car does what the model predicts. With a tank that cools as it empties, the PID brakes gently from high up and spends gas the tank cannot replace. By the last metres the tank is below the regulator's 20 MPa and gives 1.9 g at full throttle instead of 3.3, so every valve opening delivers less thrust than the law asks for. The MPC falls first and brakes late, while the tank still gives 3.2 g. Pick a case, press play, or drag the time bar.</figcaption></figure>

| PID sink-rate law | lands at 1.3 m/s, 127 kg | touches down at 2.6 m/s, 126 kg |
| MPC, fuel-optimal re-plan | lands at 1.4 m/s, 82 kg | lands at 1.4 m/s, 89 kg |

@@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S14.p6" data-s="0" data-ev>@@The comparison favours the MPC in one way: the plant here is the same point-mass model it plans with, and its model of the tank is exact.@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S14.p6" data-s="1">@@A real MPC plans with an imperfect model and relies on re-planning to absorb the difference.@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S14.p6" data-s="2" data-ev>@@The MPC lands softly on the cooling tank because it plans with the thrust the tank will still have, which a real system reads from the tank's pressure and temperature.@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S14.p6" data-s="3" data-ev>@@A PID could be given the same reading, by scheduling its sink-rate law on the tank pressure, but it would still not plan; it reacts to the speed it sees now.@@html:</span>@@

@@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S14.p7" data-s="0" data-ev>@@Neither controller can land the second stunt.@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S14.p7" data-s="1" data-ev>@@From the tank the first stunt leaves, cold, the thrusters can give at most 1.1 g once the car is upright again, barely enough to hover, and the softest touchdown any thrust history allows is 13 m/s.@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S14.p7" data-s="2">@@The PID finds that out at the ground.@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S14.p7" data-s="3" data-ev>@@The MPC's first plan is already infeasible, so a car running it would know before it committed to the stunt.@@html:</span>@@

@@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S14.p8" data-s="0" data-ev>@@Under the guidance there is still an attitude loop, the layer that turns the car to the orientation the guidance asks for, and it may well look like the PID in this post or be a linear-quadratic regulator[fn:: A linear-quadratic regulator, or LQR, takes its gains from a linear model of the vehicle: they minimise a weighted sum of the squared tracking error and the squared control effort. The PID in this post is tuned by placing its poles; an LQR's gains follow from the weights instead.], written on quaternions (four numbers that describe any orientation without the singularity Euler angles have at 90° of pitch) and with feed-forward from the plan.@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S14.p8" data-s="1" data-ev>@@Below it, an allocation layer decides which nozzles fire and for how long; for on/off thrusters that is usually pulse-width or pulse-width-pulse-frequency modulation[fn:: An on/off valve cannot open halfway. Pulse-width modulation opens it for a fraction of each short period, so that the average thrust over the period equals the command; pulse-width-pulse-frequency modulation also varies the period.], or a small linear or mixed-integer programme[fn:: A linear programme finds the values that minimise a linear cost under linear constraints: here, which nozzles to fire to make the commanded force and torque with the least gas. In a mixed-integer programme some of the values must be whole numbers, which can encode that a valve is either open or shut.] [cite:@wie2008space].@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S14.p8" data-s="2">@@Around everything, a state estimator, usually a Kalman filter that weighs a model's prediction against noisy measurements, fuses the readings of the inertial measurement unit (IMU), the wheels, the ranging sensors and the tank's pressure gauge.@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S14.p8" data-s="3" data-ev>@@The PID is the part that is easy to explain; the guidance above it is the part that lands the car softly with a tank that is running out.@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S14.p8" data-s="4" data-ev>@@That is the part I would call the hard one.@@html:</span>@@

* Conclusions

@@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S15.p1" data-s="0" data-ev>@@Tesla's numbers hold up.@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S15.p1" data-s="1">@@With the 2 350 kg that the downforce gauge and the stated 2 g of suction imply, the fans let the car crawl around the half loop with a margin of about 1.7 on grip.@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S15.p1" data-s="2" data-ev>@@The 600-litre tank holds 297 kg of supercritical nitrogen, enough for one stunt: the tank drops below the regulator's 20 MPa after a third to a half of its gas, and a stunt uses about half.@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S15.p1" data-s="3" data-ev>@@A refill takes at least 49 kWh, and the six to seven hours that Hagerty quotes suggest that the compressor is not in the car.@@html:</span>@@

@@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S15.p2" data-s="0" data-ev>@@The measured roll does not fit Tesla's list of nozzles.@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S15.p2" data-s="1">@@Rolling on the corner thrusters alone would push the car toward the ground hard enough for the gauge to read at least 1.1 g, and the gauge reads about 0.2 g.@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S15.p2" data-s="2" data-ev>@@The car therefore makes most of its roll torque some other way, which I model as an inferred couple @@html:<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>&#x003C4;</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></mrow></math>@@.@@html:</span>@@

@@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S15.p3" data-s="0" data-ev>@@In simulation a PID loop flies both stunts and follows the gauge altitude closely.@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S15.p3" data-s="1" data-ev>@@It fails with large latency, heavy sensor noise, the corner thrusters alone or a tank that cools as it empties, because it reacts to the error it sees and does not plan.@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S15.p3" data-s="2" data-ev>@@A model-predictive descent that plans with the thrust the tank will have uses 82 kg of nitrogen against the PID's 127 kg with a warm tank, and with a cooling tank it still lands at 1.4 m/s while the PID's touchdown speed rises to 2.6 m/s.@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S15.p3" data-s="3">@@From the tank the first stunt leaves, neither controller can land a second.@@html:</span>@@

@@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S15.p4" data-s="0" data-ev>@@The forces and the gas are ordinary physics.@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S15.p4" data-s="1" data-ev>@@The hard part is the guidance above the attitude loop, which has to plan a descent while the tank's thrust falls.@@html:</span>@@

* How this was made

@@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S16.p1" data-s="0" data-ev>@@The analysis is a small Python project.@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S16.p1" data-s="1" data-ev>@@The gauges are read by matching their glyphs against the labelled clusters described above, the nitrogen comes from CoolProp [cite:@bell2014coolprop], the stunts from a planar simulator written for this post, and the convex descent from cvxpy [cite:@diamond2016cvxpy], solved with Clarabel [cite:@goulart2024clarabel].@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S16.p1" data-s="2" data-ev>@@Every number in the text is filled in from those outputs when the page is built.@@html:</span>@@ @@html:<span class="zs" data-u="S16.p1" data-s="3">@@The simulators on this page are a line-by-line JavaScript port of the Python simulator, checked against it on eleven cases to six significant figures.@@html:</span>@@

<script>
var RoadsterSim = (function () {
  "use strict";
  var G0 = 9.80665;
  var DEG = Math.PI / 180;   // Python math.radians multiplies by pi/180
  var RAD = 180 / Math.PI;

  var BLOWDOWN = [[1.0, 293.15, 68.95], [0.95, 280.2, 57.6], [0.9, 267.69, 47.94], [0.85, 255.5, 39.8],
    [0.8, 243.7, 32.89], [0.75, 232.2, 27.1], [0.7, 221.04, 22.28], [0.65, 210.1, 18.2],
    [0.6, 199.5, 14.9], [0.55, 189.0, 12.1], [0.5, 178.74, 9.8], [0.45, 168.5, 7.9],
    [0.4, 158.3, 6.27], [0.35, 147.9, 4.9], [0.3, 137.46, 3.8]];

  var DEFAULTS = {
    scenario: "kickflip", mass: 2350.0, inertia: 1065.0, arm: 0.85, side_max: 38000.0,
    rcs: true, rcs_max: 30000.0, rcs_arm: 0.9, ve: 656.0,
    kp: 64.0, ki: 40.0, kd: 12.0, feedforward: true, i_limit: 0.5,
    reference: "measured", turn_start: 0.45, turn_time: 1.8,
    launch_g: 3.3, launch_time: 0.44, coast_g: 0.215, coast_world: true,
    z0: 20.6, a0_deg: 170.0, vh0: -2.5, push_g: 0.44, push_time: 0.55,
    brake_g: 1.6, z_gate: 3.0, v_gate: -2.0, tilt_gain: 0.08, tilt_max_deg: 10.0,
    lat_hold: false, pos_gain: 0.04,
    land_v: -1.0, land_kv: 4.0, land_ki: 2.0,
    dt: 0.001, ctrl_dt: 0.01, valve_tau: 0.03, delay: 0.0, onoff: false, corner_max: 19000.0,
    blowdown: false, tank_kg: 297.0, tank_start: 1.0, p_reg: 20.0,
    torque_bias: 1500.0, gust: 3000.0, gust_t: 1.2, noise_deg: 0.5, seed: 7, t_end: 7.0,
    ref_t: [], ref_a: []
  };

  function minJerk(s) {
    s = Math.min(Math.max(s, 0), 1);
    return [10 * Math.pow(s, 3) - 15 * Math.pow(s, 4) + 6 * Math.pow(s, 5),
            30 * Math.pow(s, 2) - 60 * Math.pow(s, 3) + 30 * Math.pow(s, 4),
            60 * s - 180 * Math.pow(s, 2) + 120 * Math.pow(s, 3)];
  }

  function interp(x, xs, ys) {
    if (x <= xs[0]) return ys[0];
    if (x >= xs[xs.length - 1]) return ys[ys.length - 1];
    var lo = 0, hi = xs.length - 1;
    while (hi - lo > 1) {
      var mid = Math.floor((lo + hi) / 2);
      if (xs[mid] <= x) lo = mid; else hi = mid;
    }
    var f = (x - xs[lo]) / (xs[hi] - xs[lo]);
    return ys[lo] + f * (ys[hi] - ys[lo]);
  }

  function reference(t, p) {
    if (p.reference === "measured" && p.ref_t.length) {
      var h = 0.01;
      var a = interp(t, p.ref_t, p.ref_a);
      var ap = interp(t + h, p.ref_t, p.ref_a);
      var am = interp(t - h, p.ref_t, p.ref_a);
      return [a, (ap - 2 * a + am) / (h * h)];
    }
    var mj = minJerk((t - p.turn_start) / p.turn_time);
    if (p.scenario === "kickflip") {
      return [2 * Math.PI * mj[0], 2 * Math.PI * mj[2] / Math.pow(p.turn_time, 2)];
    }
    var a0 = p.a0_deg * DEG;
    return [a0 * (1 - mj[0]), -a0 * mj[2] / Math.pow(p.turn_time, 2)];
  }

  function Lcg(seed) { this.s = seed >>> 0; }
  Lcg.prototype.uniform = function () {
    this.s = (Math.imul(1664525, this.s) + 1013904223) >>> 0;
    return this.s / 4294967296;
  };
  Lcg.prototype.gauss = function () {
    var u1 = Math.max(this.uniform(), 1e-12);
    return Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(u1)) * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * this.uniform());
  };

  function tankState(frac) {
    var rev = BLOWDOWN.slice().reverse();
    var xs = rev.map(function (b) { return b[0]; });
    return [interp(frac, xs, rev.map(function (b) { return b[1]; })),
            interp(frac, xs, rev.map(function (b) { return b[2]; }))];
  }

  function pyRound(x) {
    var r = Math.round(x);
    if (Math.abs(x % 1) === 0.5 && r % 2 !== 0) r -= 1;
    return r;
  }

  function allocate(collective, tau, arm, cap) {
    var half = tau / (2 * arm);
    var fa = collective / 2 - half, fb = collective / 2 + half;
    if (fa < 0) { fa = 0.0; fb = tau > 0 ? Math.abs(tau) / arm : 0.0; }
    if (fb < 0) { fa = tau < 0 ? Math.abs(tau) / arm : 0.0; fb = 0.0; }
    return [Math.min(Math.max(fa, 0.0), cap), Math.min(Math.max(fb, 0.0), cap)];
  }

  function nearest(levels, want) {
    var best = levels[0];
    for (var i = 1; i < levels.length; i++) {
      if (Math.abs(want - levels[i]) < Math.abs(want - best)) best = levels[i];
    }
    return best;
  }

  function simulate(opts) {
    var p = {}, k;
    for (k in DEFAULTS) p[k] = DEFAULTS[k];
    for (k in (opts || {})) p[k] = opts[k];
    var m = p.mass, inertia = p.inertia;
    var rng = new Lcg(p.seed);
    var h, z, a, vh, vz, om;
    if (p.scenario === "kickflip") { h = z = a = vh = vz = om = 0.0; }
    else { h = 0.0; z = p.z0; a = p.a0_deg * DEG; vh = p.vh0; vz = 0.0; om = 0.0; }
    var f = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0], cmd = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0], sd = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0], queue = [];
    var integ = 0.0, vinteg = 0.0, prevErr = null, gas = 0.0;
    var phase = p.scenario === "kickflip" ? "launch" : "push";
    var aMeas = a;
    var nCtrl = Math.round(p.ctrl_dt / p.dt);
    var nDelay = Math.round(p.delay / p.ctrl_dt);
    var log = { t: [], h: [], z: [], a: [], a_ref: [], fa: [], fb: [], rcs: [], gas: [], sf: [] };
    var maxErr = 0.0, sqErr = 0.0, nErr = 0, peakSf = 0.0, zmax = 0.0, touchdown = null;
    var t = 0.0, step = 0, scale = 1.0, ve = p.ve;

    while (t < p.t_end) {
      if (p.blowdown) {
        var ts = tankState(Math.max(0.3, p.tank_start - gas / p.tank_kg));
        scale = Math.min(1.0, ts[1] / p.p_reg);  // thrust = C_F p A_t: pressure, not temperature
        ve = p.ve * Math.sqrt(ts[0] / 293.15);
      }
      if (step % nCtrl === 0) {
        aMeas = a + (p.noise_deg * DEG) * rng.gauss();
        var rr = reference(t, p), ref = rr[0], refAcc = rr[1];
        if (phase === "land" && (p.scenario === "lander" || p.lat_hold)) {
          var tmax = p.tilt_max_deg * DEG;
          var want = p.tilt_gain * vh + (p.lat_hold ? p.pos_gain * h : 0.0);
          var tilt = Math.max(-tmax, Math.min(tmax, want));
          var base = p.scenario === "lander" ? 0.0 : 2 * Math.PI * pyRound(ref / (2 * Math.PI));
          ref = base + tilt; refAcc = 0.0;
        }
        var err = ref - aMeas;
        var derr = prevErr === null ? 0.0 : (err - prevErr) / p.ctrl_dt;
        prevErr = err;
        integ = Math.max(-p.i_limit, Math.min(p.i_limit, integ + err * p.ctrl_dt));
        var tau = inertia * (p.kp * err + p.ki * integ + p.kd * derr + (p.feedforward ? refAcc : 0.0));

        if (p.scenario === "kickflip") {
          if (phase === "launch" && t >= p.launch_time) phase = "coast";
          if (phase === "coast" && t > p.turn_start + p.turn_time && vz < 0) phase = "land";
        } else {
          if (phase === "push" && t >= p.push_time) phase = "flip";
          if (phase === "flip" && Math.abs(aMeas) < 20 * DEG) phase = "land";
        }
        var c = Math.cos(aMeas), collective;
        if (phase === "launch") {
          collective = m * G0 * p.launch_g;
        } else if (phase === "push") {
          collective = m * G0 * p.push_g;
        } else if (phase === "coast" || (phase === "flip" && c <= 0.3)) {
          collective = p.scenario === "kickflip" ? (c > 0.866 ? m * G0 * p.coast_g / c : 0.0) : 0.0;
        } else {
          var vref, accFf;
          if (p.scenario === "lander") {
            if (z > p.z_gate) {
              vref = -Math.sqrt(p.v_gate * p.v_gate + 2 * p.brake_g * G0 * (z - p.z_gate));
              accFf = p.brake_g * G0;
            } else {
              vref = p.land_v + (p.v_gate - p.land_v) * Math.max(z, 0.0) / p.z_gate;
              accFf = 0.0;
            }
          } else {
            vref = p.land_v - 1.2 * z;
            accFf = 0.0;
          }
          var verr = vref - vz;
          vinteg = Math.max(-2.0, Math.min(2.0, vinteg + verr * p.ctrl_dt));
          var accel = G0 + accFf + p.land_kv * verr + p.land_ki * vinteg;
          collective = c > 0.3 ? m * accel / c : 0.0;
        }
        var tRcs = p.rcs ? Math.max(-p.rcs_max, Math.min(p.rcs_max, tau)) : 0.0;
        var rest = tau - tRcs;
        var ab = allocate(collective, (c > 0.3 || !p.rcs) ? rest : 0.0, p.arm, p.side_max);
        cmd = [ab[0], ab[1], tRcs];
        if (p.onoff) {
          var levF = [0.0, p.corner_max, 2 * p.corner_max];
          var rcsStep = p.rcs_max / 2;
          var levT = [-p.rcs_max, -rcsStep, 0.0, rcsStep, p.rcs_max];
          var out = [];
          for (var q = 0; q < 3; q++) {
            var want = cmd[q] + sd[q];
            var lev = nearest(q < 2 ? levF : levT, want);
            sd[q] = want - lev;
            out.push(lev);
          }
          cmd = out;
        }
        queue.push(cmd);
        cmd = queue.length > nDelay ? queue.shift() : [0.0, 0.0, 0.0];
      }

      var kv = p.dt / p.valve_tau;
      f = [f[0] + kv * (cmd[0] * scale - f[0]), f[1] + kv * (cmd[1] * scale - f[1]), f[2] + kv * (cmd[2] * scale - f[2])];
      var bigF = f[0] + f[1];
      var torque = (f[1] - f[0]) * p.arm + f[2];
      var dist = p.torque_bias + ((p.gust_t <= t && t < p.gust_t + 0.3) ? p.gust : 0.0);
      var coastLift = (p.coast_world && phase === "coast" && Math.cos(a) <= 0.866) ? p.coast_g * G0 : 0.0;
      var ah = -bigF * Math.sin(a) / m;
      var az = bigF * Math.cos(a) / m - G0 + coastLift;
      var alpha = (torque + dist) / inertia;
      vh += ah * p.dt; vz += az * p.dt; om += alpha * p.dt;
      h += vh * p.dt; z += vz * p.dt; a += om * p.dt;
      gas += (bigF + Math.abs(f[2]) / p.rcs_arm + m * coastLift) / ve * p.dt;
      t += p.dt;
      step += 1;

      var refNow = reference(t, p)[0];
      if (p.scenario === "kickflip" || phase !== "land") {
        var e = refNow - a;
        maxErr = Math.max(maxErr, Math.abs(e));
        sqErr += e * e;
        nErr += 1;
      }
      peakSf = Math.max(peakSf, bigF / m / G0);
      if (step % 10 === 0) {
        log.t.push(t); log.h.push(h); log.z.push(z); log.a.push(a); log.a_ref.push(refNow);
        log.fa.push(f[0]); log.fb.push(f[1]); log.rcs.push(f[2]); log.gas.push(gas); log.sf.push(Math.hypot(ah, az + G0) / G0);
      }
      zmax = Math.max(zmax, z);
      if (z <= 0 && zmax > 0.5 && t > 0.3) {
        var turns = Math.round(a / (2 * Math.PI));
        touchdown = { t: t, vz: vz, vh: vh, a_deg: (a - 2 * Math.PI * turns) * RAD, h: h };
        break;
      }
    }
    var apex = 0;
    for (var i = 0; i < log.z.length; i++) apex = Math.max(apex, log.z[i]);
    return {
      params: p,
      metrics: { gas_kg: gas, max_err_deg: maxErr * RAD, rms_err_deg: Math.sqrt(sqErr / Math.max(nErr, 1)) * RAD,
                 peak_g: peakSf, apex_m: log.z.length ? apex : 0.0, touchdown: touchdown },
      log: log
    };
  }

  return { simulate: simulate, DEFAULTS: DEFAULTS, G0: G0 };
})();
